title: Process of adding a sailing feature to my Fishing RPG
author: ForkedPush
selftext:
With the arrival of Fable 5.2, I decided to add the sailing feature I have been itching to add to my game.

When I add a new mechanic to my game, I first add it with the bare minimum polish: primitive shapes, no fancy animation, no SFX or VFX. This way I can quickly test the new mechanic without any distraction, and this first pass shows me the problems sooner. For example, when I piloted the ship the shoulder camera saw the whole island and the frame rate dropped. It also helped me figure out the best size for the ship. This way I only needed Fable 5.2 to build the detailed ship once. After that I used Opus 5.5 to fix small problems and make some changes. Most of this applies to a workflow without AI too. Trying out new stuff with primitive blocks is a good rule of thumb in my experience.

Here I used Claude + Blender MCP + Unity. I am still not a fan of the camera view/controls on the  ship. Trying to figure out the best approach for it. If you have any suggestions feel free to tell me. No matter how small it is, it might give me a clue.

I Just Wanted to Fish is a game I have been working on for almost two months. It has a free demo on Steam, feel free to check it out.

Steam link: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5351000/I\_Just\_Wanted\_to\_Fish\_Demo/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5351000/I_Just_Wanted_to_Fish_Demo/)

Thanks! Honestly I have been brain storming on the core fishing mechanic in my game. It gets stale after catching a few fish. I was playing many different fishing games to get an idea to what makes them fun even after you catch many. New World's fishing mechanics looks good but I am curious what that monster bass is about. Is it playable today?

Since this is the core mechanic and fun factor of my game I want to get it right
